Derek Chang: Upload model runbook, batch/kv-cache settings, and quantization flags used during test (due 2026-03-11)

meeting_header: Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Derek Chang (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Snowcap CTO), Ethan Brooks (Snowcap Lead ML Eng), Priya Nair (Snowcap SRE)
summary: Weekly POC check-in to compare Redwood test runs vs incumbent provider. Redwood showed consistent lower p50 and p95 latency and higher sustained throughput in current workload. Discussed batch/quantization tradeoffs, KV/prefix cache behavior, and potential network peering constraints. Agreed next steps to exchange raw traces and for customer to run a 10k-sample latency audit; team to evaluate dedicated slot if RPS needs exceed thresholds.
topics: Throughput (RPS) saturation curves and RPS targets
Effect of batching and quantization on latency and quality
Networking constraints (VPC peering, egress) and test harness impacts
Next steps: traces, configs, dedicated capacity sizing
transcript: [00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: Maya here, hi Samira, Ethan, Priya on the line as well.
[00:15] Samira: Great, Derek from our side and I'll run through the numbers we collected late last night. Apologies, a couple of the file names got long so i annotated them.

[00:30] Derek: Quick note, some of the recorded metrics that we pushed to the bucket were from the int8 quant runs and a second run without quant so you'll see both — i labeled them int8 and fp16 in the CSV.
[00:45] Ethan: Cool, that helps. We were particularly keen on p95 for 512-token prompts because that's what our customers hit in production.

[00:58] Samira: Right. So headline: Redwood baseline in our harness—p50 ~42ms, p95 ~190ms for the 512-token sim. Incumbent provider in your prior tests sat at p50 ~60ms, p95 ~320ms under the same synthetic traffic shape. Throughput: Redwood sustained about 180 RPS before crossing the 250ms tail threshold; incumbent crossed it around 140 RPS.

[01:25] Maya: Hmm those numbers look promising, especially the p95 improvement. Were both runs using the same batching settings? Sometimes their SDK enforces big batches by default so i wanna make sure it's apples to apples.

[01:40] Derek: Good call. We matched effective max batch latency to 25ms and capped max batch size at 8 for the Redwood run. For the incumbent run we set identical client-side batch windows but their runtime still aggregated differently — note in the CSV the realized batch size distribution was ~6.4 mean for incumbent vs ~5.1 mean for Redwood.
[02:05] Priya: Are you seeing warmup effects? Our prod traffic is bursty and small prefixes repeat often; caching could matter a lot.

[02:14] Derek: Yes, warmup mattered. We ran a 10k warmup sequence to bring the KV/prefix cache to steady state; without warmup p95 spiked to ~480ms. With warmup, the prefix cache cut tail by roughly 60%. We also observed the prefix cache eviction chatter on the incumbent side — likely smaller KV caps.
[02:40] Ethan: Any sign that quantization (int8) is hurting output quality? We have strict QA thresholds before we'll accept a lower-cost profile.

[02:49] Samira: We ran the standard redwood-eval harness on the outputs — int8 introduced about a 1.8% BLEU/semantic drop on our prompts for this model, fp16 was baseline. We captured diff examples in the artifacts bucket, i'll include a short report.
[03:05] Maya: That is tolerable depending on cost delta. What's the unit cost difference you're projecting at these throughput levels?

[03:13] Samira: Rough back-of-envelope: at steady 150 RPS int8 path reduces per-token cost ~28% vs fp16 on our infra profile. Against the incumbent's profile, total unit cost was about 22% lower when we factor in fewer tokens lost to timeouts and retries since ttfb is lower.
[03:30] Priya: Network was a bottleneck during one of our earlier runs when we generated load from an external tester — could that have biased the incumbent numbers?

[03:39] Derek: We saw 5–10ms variance tied to egress routing in one of the zones; we flagged those segments. For the CSV we excluded the runs where external network jitter >15ms. I'll annotate which zone those were — it was us-west-2 test harness.
[03:58] Ethan: On throughput, you mentioned 180 RPS sustained. What's the behavior at 200–240 RPS? Is it a hard drop-off or graceful ramping of tail latencies?

[04:08] Derek: Past 180 RPS we start to see p95 climb nonlinear — 200 RPS gives p95 ~260ms, 220 RPS ~350ms; at 240RPS the service starts rejecting some requests indicating QPS limits on that config. We can tune autoscale/faster queueing or propose reserved slots for guaranteed throughput.
[04:28] Maya: Could reserved capacity be cheaper than us managing retries at the app layer?

[04:34] Samira: Often yes — reserved slots reduce jitter and you avoid the cost of overprovisioning upstream. We'll run a sizing calc, but for Snowcap's peak patterns we estimate 4 dedicated slots would give steady 220 RPS headroom with 20% buffer.
[04:50] Ethan: What about cold start for model variants? We sometimes route rare variants and the cold start cost is a concern.

[04:58] Derek: Our runtime supports quick warming via KV cache prefetch and continuous batching; cold start for the same family is ~2–4 seconds for full model load unless pinned. If you need sub-500ms always-on for that rare path we recommend pinning or warm containers — that's what dedicated does.
[05:16] Priya: SSO/policy side — any limitation on audit logs or retention we should know about during evaluation?

[05:23] Samira: For pilot we provide 90 days of request/response metadata plus token-level cost breakdown. For enterprise private we can extend retention and integrate with your KMS; I'll attach SOC2/ISO docs as well.
[05:36] Maya: Great. A little nit — in the CSV there are a couple of label mismatches where model name is truncated (redwood-35 -> redwood35). Could you fix that for our ingestion?
[05:46] Derek: Yep absolutely. That's a labeling script issue on our side, will push fixed CSVs with consistent names.
[05:55] Ethan: How deterministic are the p95 numbers? If we re-run the same batch of 50k prompts will the p95 be similar?

[06:04] Derek: Within +/-12% for p95 given the same harness, but if network or cache warmup changes it can swing more. That's why we recommended your 10k-sample audit to be run from your prod VPC to capture real network dynamics.
[06:22] Maya: Let's talk about regressions — we need a guardrail if a new model or quant profile regresses quality by more than 2%. Does Redwood have eval hooks?

[06:31] Samira: Yes, Optimize integrates evals and can block rollout if quality metrics drop below your threshold. For pilot we can gate canary traffic on the eval results and keep rollback policies simple.
[06:44] Priya: Any suggestions on the synthetic harness we should run? We currently run ramp + steady + spike. Do you have a recommended schedule?
[06:52] Derek: We suggested a three-phase run: 10k warmup, 30k steady-state at target RPS, a 5k burst spike to 10x for autoscaling observation. We'll share the exact k6 scripts we used.
[07:06] Ethan: On metric deltas, can you call out p50/p95 delta lines in the CSV? I want a quick filter to show only the deltas vs incumbent.
[07:14] Samira: Done — the CSV column named delta_p95_vs_incumbent is included. For a high-level read: median p95 improvement across payloads ~ 35–42% depending on prompt length.
[07:28] Maya: There's an odd spike logged around run 23 — looks like eviction churn. Could that be memory pressure?
[07:35] Derek: Likely. We saw GC/eviction logs on the incumbent runs. On Redwood the kernel selection and kv cache sizing avoided that churn in our tests.
[07:47] Priya: If we wanted to run a head-to-head inside our VPC are there credentials or a sandbox we should use?
[07:54] Samira: Yes — we'll provide a short-lived API key and a pre-built harness you can run from a bastion. We'll also give an IAM role pattern for the VPC peering. Derek will attach the steps.
[08:06] Ethan: Regarding the quantization flags, can we see the exact command line? We need to replicate exactly for our offline QA.
[08:12] Derek: Yes, action item noted — I'll paste the quantize command and the exact kernel flags in the artifact bundle.
[08:20] Maya: One of our concerns is error modes — did you see more 5xx errors at high RPS on Redwood vs incumbent?

[08:27] Derek: During the sustained runs Redwood had near-zero 5xx until we hit resource queueing at 240RPS — incumbent's 5xx started earlier around 180RPS. We'll include the 5xx counts in the trace dump.
[08:39] Ethan: For the ticket we'll want a breakdown by route — inference vs preproc vs postproc. Can the CSV separate those latencies?
[08:46] Samira: Yes all latencies are broken into ttfb, model_gen, and app_postproc columns.
[08:52] Priya: Any gotchas with timezones or clock sync when you ran distributed load generators? We've had mismatched clocks hurt traces before.
[09:00] Derek: We NTP-synced everything and used monotonic timestamps; the artifact header includes the ntp offset. We filtered runs where offset exceeded 50ms.
[09:10] Maya: Can you restate recommended config for Snowcap's pattern? Short bullet list would help.

[09:16] Samira: Sure — recommended pilot config: reserved 4 slots for peak 220RPS headroom, max_batch_latency 25ms, max_batch_size 8, prefix/KV cache sized to 50k keys, int8 profile for cost experiments but gate with evals. We'll send this as a succinct doc.
[09:35] Ethan: If we move to reserved slots, what's the SLA difference? Any changes to p95 windows?

[09:42] Samira: Reserved capacity reduces variance — you'd typically see p95 drop 10–20ms in our tests and far fewer tail spikes; SLA is documented in the addendum and we can share the reserved slot contract example.
[09:58] Priya: We're aiming to decide by the end of next week whether to expand pilot or start an internal bake period. Is that timeline feasible?
[10:05] Samira: Yes, if you run the 10k audit by Monday and we get traces by Tuesday we can size reserved slots and present the cost model by Thursday.
[10:14] Maya: Perfect. Anything else on the test artifacts?

[10:19] Derek: I'll include the raw p95 histograms, the k6 scripts, and the exact runtime flags. Also, one more note — in one test we saw slightly higher memory use when using certain kernel combos; we documented which kernel picks led to the best latency/throughput tradeoff.
[10:34] Ethan: We will run the 10k audit from our staging VPC and share the results. Also will test with our real small-burst traffic pattern.
[10:41] Priya: I'll open a ticket with our infra team for peering and give a target window for the load run.
[10:46] Samira: Awesome. Quick recap of next steps: Samira/Derek share artifacts and scripts; Ethan/Priya run audit and return traces; Redwood proposes reserved slot sizing if needed. Any blockers?
[10:56] Maya: No blockers from product side. Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[11:02] Samira: Thanks — will follow up with the CSV and a short slide summarizing the delta. Bye all.
[11:08] (call ends)
